source.anchor_kjv: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,
source.thread: "made of a woman" — Paul's one deliberate phrase, four thousand years after a promise spoken over a woman in a garden
source.hook_line: You've heard it as Plan B — Eden fell apart, so God improvised a rescue and sent His Son.
source.spoken_script: You've heard it as Plan B — Eden fell apart, so God improvised a rescue and sent His Son. That is not what the oldest promise says. Genesis already named this seed — a promise spoken over a woman in the garden. Jesus wasn't a rescue invented in the fulness of time. He was the plan, named first. Paul writes: 'But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law.' Paul could have written son of David, son of Abraham — a line that runs through the man, like every title before it. Here, he doesn't. He writes: made of a woman, the woman promised in the garden. You still reach for your own rescue plans — the fix, the resolution, the version of you that finally gets it right. But the plan was never yours to write. This was never Plan B. It was the plan, kept word for word — and He has already arrived for you.

platforms.description:
You may have heard it as Plan B: Eden fell apart, so God improvised a rescue. That is not what the oldest promise says. Genesis already named this seed.

"But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law," (Galatians 4:4, KJV)

Paul could have written son of David or son of Abraham. He wrote made of a woman, the woman promised in the garden. Jesus was not a rescue invented later. He was the plan, named first, kept word for word.

The plan was never yours to write, and He has already arrived for you.
